decisions.reason: As a generic add-on web service with weak strategic distinctiveness, it is more likely to fall below aspiration levels and be discontinued despite the firm's current slack.
Because it is close to the firm's data-driven core offer, the firm is expanding, and some slack exists to sustain a niche product while demand is tested, management would more likely keep it.
This service fits the firm's regulated energy-process expertise and platform direction, so in the absence of clear failure its performance likely meets aspirations well enough to retain it.
A tariff database is strongly related to the firm's established data and compliance business, and a multi-model product line would usually be kept unless results clearly disappointed.

Although related to the existing offer, custom web services are less aligned with the move toward standardized SaaS modules, so management is somewhat more likely to reallocate resources if returns are not clearly satisfactory.

A postal code lookup service looks like a low-differentiation utility outside the firm's higher-value core, making it the kind of offer a boundedly rational management would drop first when reviewing fit and payoff.
